findings.title: NAV-anchored exit floor lets an unprivileged actor cheaply revert a pending exit, skim, or migration by front-running with a Curve pool dump (transient griefing)
findings.description: minOut = convertToAssets(shares)*(1-bps) is anchored to sUSDe NAV. The AMM exit price sits below NAV, so the margin under the guard is thin: live headroom is ~23.8 bps under the 30 bps tolerance (router get_dy for the strategy's 5,162 sUSDe = 6,475.75 USDe vs floor 6,460.34). A public-mempool exit can be sandwiched: dump sUSDe into the crvUSD/sUSDe pool, let the victim exit revert on the router's _expected check, then buy back. Fork probe: a 250k-sUSDe dump reverts a strategy-shaped exit for a round-trip cost of ~101 sUSDe (~$127). The capital must be held across the bundle, not flash-loaned. The same lever applies to skimSurplus and the Phase-2 totalWithdrawal execution. MR-003 donation variant: moving sUSDe NAV by the 24 bps headroom means donating ~0.24% of totalAssets (1.19e27 wei, ~1.19B USDe), ~$2.8M given away to every sUSDe holder. Not credible. DISTINCT from M-02 d7f6c2dfd580 / M-01-run12 fdda8f53151a, which are value-leak sandwich framings already judged false-positive: here the guard WORKS and no value is extracted, the impact is a revert. DISTINCT from L-22 7a66fe7d5a96, whose premise was the deleted quote. Persistent DoS only arises from the natural NAV-vs-pool lag under default/low bps, which is L-01 6460e35331df's root cause and owner-recoverable via setSlippageTolerance.
findings.severityRationale: Transient and per-transaction. The attacker profits nothing and pays per grief. Victims retry, or the owner and clients use a private mempool. This is inherent to any slippage-guarded swap, and C4 treats it as QA/invalid. Kept visible per Law 1, not as H/M.

findings.title: Operational hazard: the live mainnet CurveAMMAdapter 0x2D02…D6f runs the pre-story-052 setRoute; HEAD's contiguity guarantee does not apply to the deployed adapter the live USDe strategy is bound to
findings.description: YieldStrategyUSDe 0xaC2e5936Eca286eC364d4D5Bcca33145fBe57f95 holds ammAdapter = 0x2D024e0d03Fb6Ead4F8E7Ba1EBECF6db0E755D6f (immutable, so it cannot be repointed). That adapter is a non-proxy deployment of the old code, so any owner setRoute there still accepts the M-01 gapped shape. VERIFIED CURRENT STATE IS SAFE. (1) The full RouteSet history from deploy (OwnershipTransferred at block 25283688) contains exactly two events: USDe->sUSDe at block 25283690 and sUSDe->USDe at block 25283691. (2) Both stored routes (getRoute) are contiguous 2-hop routes that pass every HEAD check. (3) Their i/j indices match pool coins: F55B… coins [USDe, crvUSD]; 5706… coins [crvUSD, sUSDe]. (4) Self-pairs are not configured. CALL-SITE ENUMERATION (phoenix-phase-2-staging @ d0060cb, full grep): the only first-party CurveAMMAdapter.setRoute callers are script/archives/MigrateStableStakerMainnet.s.sol:454,464 and script/archives/interactions/governance/DeployUSDeMarketYieldStrategy.s.sol:143,165. Both are archived, neither is wired in package.json, and both payloads are contiguous and equal src/AMMRoutes.json. script/helpers/SyaHarvesterLocalConfig.sol:68 targets SYAHarvester, not this adapter. DeployMocks*.s.sol use MockMarketAMMAdapter (UI mock). No pending or committed script pushes a gapped route. The archived script's NatSpec at MigrateStableStakerMainnet.s.sol:441-442 still describes the old 'last non-zero == tokenOut' check, which is accurate for the live adapter and would mislead nobody reading it. Footgun test: an owner who reads HEAD source and the story-052 closure could assume contiguity is enforced on mainnet. The vault CLAUDE.md documents the divergence, which lowers the surprise.
findings.severityRationale: No live harm and no pending trigger. If realised (a gapped reverse route on mainnet) the impact is exit reverts or crvUSD delivered to the strategy. That is Medium-shaped but depends on a future owner misconfig, so it is an operational hazard per Law 3.

findings.title: Validator-accepted route whose path token disagrees with pool coin j: fails loudly on live Router NG (no stranding); residual of L-07 / T-3
findings.description: Focus-1 answer. HEAD pins structure, path[0]==tokenIn and path[2k]==tokenOut, so Router NG's delivered token is always tokenOut, and a structurally valid route cannot mis-deliver a wrong token to the strategy. A wrong i/j still passes setRoute (probe: [sUSDe, crvUSD/sUSDe pool, USDe] with i=1, j=0 is accepted). On the live router the swap reverts 'Received nothing', even at minOut 0, because the pool emits crvUSD while the router measures its USDe balance. With the strategy floor it also reverts. Stranding needs two conditions together: slippageToleranceBps == MAX_BPS (minOut 0) and the router holding output-token dust. Neither holds live. Cyclic routes (A->..->A->..->B) are accepted and only cost extra fees. swap_type >= 10 is LOCAL-002 (profiler). tokenIn == tokenOut is LOCAL-001. Outcome: no stranded or mis-delivered output from any accepted route under live conditions. The strategy-level effect of a bad route is a recoverable revert of deposit/withdraw/skim until the owner overwrites the route.
findings.reconcile: L-07 partially fixed: the zero-gap half is closed by story-052; the tokenIn==tokenOut and off-chain i/j halves remain. Do not mint a new fingerprint.

findings.title: L-12 coupling re-checked: live Router NG return equals the delivered balance delta; strategies forwarding the returned amount are correct under T-1
findings.description: Hand-off H-B. On fork, swap() via the live adapter returned exactly the USDe delta at msg.sender, and the adapter retained 0 of both tokens. Router NG prices each hop by its own balanceOf(output_token), so a donation to the router only over-delivers to the next swapper, which the strategy forwards harmlessly. No divergence path exists while T-1 (genuine immutable Router NG) holds. L-12 stays open as defense-in-depth. Unchanged by story-052.
findings.reconcile: still-present, unchanged code; do not re-file
